name: Bear Gap off the Highs

card.context: Taught today as a level, not a trade (TRADE_PLANS.md: the fall is measured, not traded). The short the dossier measured, Version R, lives under a flat or falling 200-day (B26), in a weak group, in an Orange or Red market. Above the 200-day only Bracco's day-2 parabolic variant could qualify, pending his ruling.
card.pattern: A 250-session closing top within the last 80 sessions, the prior close within 15% of it (better: a range near the highs). Then the first gap down since that top: an open at least 1 ATR or 4% under the prior close, not filled that day, on 1.5x volume, closing down 5% or more in the lower half.
card.trigger: No trade in the app today. Version R, if he rules it in: within 25 sessions a light bounce into the gap zone or the declining 20-day or 50-day is rejected; short at market as price trades under the rejection candle's low.
card.stop: A few cents over the rejection candle's high, within about 3%. Never over the gap day's high on a gap-day close entry: that sat a median 4.2% away and 25% on VRNS.
card.failure_mode: The gap fills: a close back above the zone's top edge. Or the first bounce is bought hard: an earnings collapse straight off a fresh high often reverses up through the stop at once (DIS 2015), and a short taken in a strong market gets run over (CIEN and CHKP 2017).

criteria.statement: Today the app defines no trade: the lesson shows the line a close must stay under, the gap day's high, and the fall is measured, not traded.
criteria.evidence: TRADE_PLANS.md: 'no trade is defined in the app | the lesson shows the line a close must stay under: the gap day's high | the fall is measured, not traded.' Course V.05 marks 'Our app defines a full short trade for the Bear gap' as False. VRNS 2025-10-29: a stop over the gap day's high sat 25.0% over the close.

criteria.statement: Is it a short at all: a level lesson only, a short setup, or both with the level first. The dossier's measured short side is Version R, the retest short below the 200-day, and it waits on the owner.

options.basis: a level lesson only (the vocabulary file, the course, how UCT writes about it)
a short setup
both, level first; the short only as Version R and Version P (the dossier's recommendation)

criteria.evidence: Shorting the gap day's close by the app's rule earned -0.02R (1,733 trades; random shorts -0.09R). The retest scan: 359 hits, 25.3% to 3R, 14.2% to 5R; the dossier's crude daily stand-in for the owner's tactic (T3) was -0.02R, so the short waits for his charts. DECISIONS D-001's default names 27's Versions R and P among the three traded shorts.

criteria.statement: A 250-session closing high (the top) set within the prior 80 sessions, and the close before the gap within 15% of it.

options.basis: the app's draft (let in NFLX 2022-01-21, already 26% down, which he cut)
the dossier's proposal
DECISIONS D-098's default

criteria.statement: Option A: any top. Option B, MPWR's shape: a range near the highs, the top 15 or more sessions earlier and the prior close within 5% of it.

measure.and: prior close within 5% of the top

a range near the highs, like MPWR (DECISIONS D-098's default)
the owner's call per chart

criteria.evidence: ChartSchool's breakaway gap comes after 'an extended top or a consolidation period'; Bulkowski's 'on leaving a consolidation area'. Scan: the top 15 or more sessions before the gap reached 3R 69 of 256 times (27%) against 22 of 103 (21%) straight off the top. Test: a range near the highs (top 20+ sessions earlier, prior close within 5%) +0.09R, 154 trades.

criteria.statement: The open is under the prior close by at least 1 ATR(14) or 4%, whichever is smaller, and the gap is not filled that day: the day's high stays under the prior close.

measure.value: min(1 ATR(14), 4% of the prior close)
measure.and: the day's high < the prior close

options.basis: a full daily window, the high under the prior low (the app now)
any open under the prior close not filled that day (the owner's BE, GLW, MRNA examples; DECISIONS D-099's default with a 1 ATR floor)
a minimum size: 5% (the app), 1 ATR, or 4%

criteria.evidence: UCT's named bear gaps (BE, GLW, MRNA, both of SNDK's) were overnight gaps, not full windows; ChartSchool's 'Partial Gap Down' is the published name. The app's 5% and true-window gates miss most of them; GLD's was 4.1%. The 1 ATR in sr_levels.py measures a full window, not the open.

criteria.statement: The stricter form, a full window: the gap day's high under the prior day's low. The app's current rule; all 10 scan examples were full windows.

measure.what: gap day's high against the prior day's low

criteria.evidence: ChartSchool's down gap and Bulkowski's falling window ('yesterday's low is above today's high'). Bulkowski: a falling window showed overhead resistance 25% of the time.

criteria.statement: The first gap of this kind since the top. Later gaps off the same top did worse.

measure.what: earlier gaps of this kind since the top

criteria.evidence: The app's draft rule. Test: off a top but not the first gap, 680 trades, -0.22R (95% range -0.36 to -0.05).

criteria.statement: At least 1.5x the 50-day average volume on the gap day; 2x for an A grade.

options.basis: the app and Fleckenstein ('at minimum double')
the dossier's proposal
none as a gate (the owner's SNDK gaps had 1.3x and 0.9x); DECISIONS D-099's default

criteria.statement: The gap day closes down at least 5% and in the lower half of its range.

criteria.statement: The gap zone: for a full window, from the gap day's high up to the prior day's low; for an overnight gap, up to the prior close. The chart draws both edges as one zone.

measure.value: gap day's high to the prior day's low (a window) or to the prior close (an overnight gap)

options.basis: draw the zone between them as one band (the dossier's recommendation; DECISIONS D-100's default)
the gap day's high only (the course text)
the prior day's low only (the overlay's gold label)

criteria.evidence: The course says the line is the gap day's high; the overlay labels the prior day's low. Sources and UCT treat the zone as resistance, and a close above the top edge fills it. SNDK's 2026-06-26 gap closed back over the prior day's low on 06-30 but never over the prior close by 07-10, which is why the owner could still call it open.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on average.
The position is at most 1% of average daily volume.
Version L: under the zone, the zone is resistance. The first rally into it is where the trapped buyers sell.
criteria.evidence: The owner on CRWV: 'The bear gap to the left just around $120 is acting as resistance.' Schaeffer's: the equity 'becomes unable to hurdle through the gap zone'; ChartSchool: a downside breakout point becomes resistance. The vocabulary file files 'Bear Gap' as a level; sr_levels.py already draws it.

criteria.statement: A close above the zone's top edge fills the gap; a quick fill is strength. The level and any short are off.

measure.what: close against the zone's top edge

criteria.evidence: QQQ: 'a major sign of strength to fill bear gaps quickly'; SPY: 'only took two sessions to negate Tuesday's bear gap'. ChartSchool and Schaeffer's on filling. The scan ended every setup on a close above the top edge.

criteria.statement: For a long: do not buy right under an open bear gap; wait for the fill or a base under it. For a holder: a bear gap off highs on your stock is a warning; manage by the trail and the gap rule (B20).

measure.what: a new long under an open bear gap
measure.value: wait for the fill or a base

criteria.evidence: The owner on MRNA: 'Don't love the big bear gap off highs on day two but a proper signal down here would be worthy of the tight risk imo.' On BE: 'Gross bear gap off highs. Would like to see some supportive action early in the week.' TSDR uses a bear gap overhead as a first trim spot on longs.

criteria.statement: Version R: the stock closes under its 200-day SMA on the setup day.
criteria.evidence: The owner: 'I want them below the 200SMA for sure'. 61% of the app's events close above the 200-day on the gap day (90% the day before), and every UCT-named example but MPWR; those are not Version R shorts. criteria.statement: Within 25 sessions of the gap, price rallies into the gap zone, or to the declining 20-day EMA or 50-day SMA, without a close above the zone's top edge.

criteria.statement: Not right after a big unwind, and never eager: 'pressing shorts immediately after an unwind like feels dangerous'; 'Do not ever be eager to short. Ever.'

criteria.statement: Not too late in the down cycle, and not after several gaps off the same top.

criteria.statement: Version R: a close back above the 200-day, or above the 50-day the bounce was rejected from.

measure.what: close against the 200-day SMA (or the rejected 50-day)

criteria.statement: A strong, high-volume bounce into the zone that closes near its high: buyers in control. Fleckenstein's opposite case; a B- or a pass.
The market reading turns Green with breadth thrusting: stand down.

Never short the gap day's close by reflex: the stop over its high is wide (median 4.2%), the stock sits far under its 10-day, and big one-day drops bounced 28% on average in Bulkowski's dead-cat sample.

measure.what: entry on the gap day's close

criteria.evidence: Test: the gap-day close short (T1) -0.02R on 1,733 trades; 43% of gap-day closes more than 10% under the 10-day. The bear-gap atlas counted the gap day's own low as profit on close entries (measure_rules.py), which flatters that entry.

criteria.evidence: The 39 drafts sit under SET.22, a long setup; Hard mode lists 'Bear gap' as its one short. DECISIONS D-016's default: 'Bear gap off the highs', its own unit, a card and a tag.

a_plus: bg.first_gap: the first gap down off a clear top, or a range near the highs (bg.structure), on 2x volume or more (bg.gap_volume), closing in the lower part of its range and through support (bg.gap_day)
bg.earnings_breakdown: a real reason, a guidance cut or an earnings collapse in a crowded growth name, but from a range, not one day off a fresh high
bg.below_200: under a flat or falling 200-day (bg.flat_falling_200); bg.weak_rs: a weak group; bg.market: a weak reading
bg.bounce: a light-volume bounce (bg.light_bounce) into the gap zone and a declining 20-day or 50-day at the same price, then a clean rejection candle (bg.rejection_candle)
bg.stop_width: a stop within 3%, with at least 5R of room to the gap-day low or the next support
bg.p_burst: Version P with most of Bracco's boxes checked, a clear hanging man or doji on the highest volume of the run (bg.p_climax_day), and a day 2 that gaps down and never fills (bg.p_day2)
b_minus: bg.first_gap: a second or third gap off the same top (bg.not_late)
bg.inv_strong_bounce: a bounce on heavy volume that pokes into the zone and closes near its high
bg.below_200: still above the 200-day (not allowed unless Version P)
bg.not_after_flush: the market just flushed and breadth is washed out
bg.stop_width: a stop wider than 3%; bg.earnings: a report within 3 days; bg.borrow: hard to borrow
bg.earnings_breakdown: a no-news drop (more likely to reverse, Savor)
bg.p_burst: Version P where the burst is a rebound from a crash low rather than a run to new highs (those drove almost all of the test's positive result)
no_trade: bg.status: as the app stands, no trade: the level is measured, not traded
bg.no_reflex_short: the gap day's close, by reflex
bg.below_200: above the 200-day, except Version P if he rules the exception covers it (bg.p_above_200)
bg.earnings_breakdown: an earnings collapse one to three sessions off a fresh high, the shape he cut
bg.no_chase: more than 4% under the trigger; bg.not_stretched: more than 10% under the 10-day
bg.earnings: a report within 3 sessions; bg.borrow: hard to borrow
bg.market: a Green or Yellow reading, or a market that just turned Green with breadth thrusting (bg.inv_market_turn)

lookalikes.tell: Read the close against the prior close. A bear gap off the highs opens down and closes down 5% or more: the bad news worked. A News Failure (long) opens down on the same bad news and closes above the prior close: the news failed, and that is a buy, not a short.

Look at the day before the gap. A Parabolic Short's main form is shorted on a climax day that gaps up and closes red after a 3 to 5 day burst; the day-2 gap down after a hanging-man climax is its smaller variant (Version P here). A plain bear gap off the highs has no burst before it and is shorted only on the later retest, below the 200-day.

Count the down days before the gap. A Parabolic Long's climax gap down comes after three straight lower closes and two gap downs, and is bought on the intraday turn; a bear gap off the highs is the first gap since the top, with the prior close still within 15% of it, and nothing is bought.

Check the 200-day and the leader. A leader above a rising 200-day that gaps down on earnings is the owner's '3 day gap down earnings reversal' buy (PLTR, CLS), Mean Reversion form A; a bear gap short lives only under the 200-day, in a weak name, after the bounce fails.
Which way did it gap? Gap Support is a gap up whose zone is tested later as support for a long; the bear gap is a gap down whose zone is resistance. Same mechanics, opposite line.

invalidations: Before any trigger: a close above the gap zone's top edge fills the gap (bg.fill).
Version R, before the trigger: a close back above the 200-day, or above the 50-day the bounce was rejected from (bg.inv_200).
Before the trigger: a strong, high-volume bounce into the zone closing near its high (bg.inv_strong_bounce).
Before the trigger: the market reading turns Green with breadth thrusting (bg.inv_market_turn).
Before the trigger: no trigger within 5 sessions of the rejection day (bg.trigger_window).
After the entry: the stop is the exit and never moves higher (bg.stop_never_wider); under 1R after 10 sessions, cover (bg.time_stop).
mistakes: Shorting the gap day's close by reflex. The stop is wide, the stock is stretched far under its 10-day, and in Bulkowski's dead-cat sample the big drops bounced 28% on average.
Shorting a leader above a rising 200-day (B26), where the owner himself buys gap-down reversals.
Shorting too late in the down cycle (Bracco), or after several gaps off the same top (later gaps did worse in the test).
Treating every big earnings drop as a bear gap off the highs. He called those 'just an earnings breakdown'.
Ignoring the fill: holding a short after a close back above the gap zone.
Chasing: shorting far under the trigger (C28 mirror).
Hard-to-borrow names and squeezes (D48; the owner's 'Mechanical short squeeze').
Sizing a variant like a main setup. Bracco: 'smaller size'.
Buying right under an open bear gap on the long side, instead of waiting for the fill or a base.
Reading the drafts as proof that bear gaps usually hold: the finder ranked gap_held first, so 37 of 39 drafts held by construction.

short_mirror.note: This card is itself a short. Its long mirror is a gap up out of a base: Gap Support (25) and the Power Earnings Gap (21). D47 says shorts are our longs reversed; Version R is the reverse of his pullback-to-a-rising-average buy ('Essentially the same tactics I use for longs but just incredibly more selective'). The opposite trade on the same chart is his '3 day gap down earnings reversal' buy in a leader early in a recovery (CLS, PLTR); the lesson shows both so a gap down in a leader is never read as an automatic short.

best_conditions: Version R: a Red or Orange reading, the stock below a flat or falling 200-day, its group weak, a light bounce into the zone and a declining 20-day or 50-day at the same price. Not right after a big flush ('Do not ever be eager to short'). Version P: any market, best when the burst is far from its averages. A Red market is not by itself an edge: the gap-day close short did worse with SPY under its 200-day.

management.trail: cover the last third on a close back above the 10-day average for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first cover by default (B19)
management.time_stop: under 1R of profit after 10 sessions, cover (C33)
management.gap_open: a cover level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: a gap up over the stop: the first 30-minute high is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.overrides: Version P takes Bracco's target, the daily 9 EMA, for at least a third (D47; D-013 pending), and is sized in the B- band ('smaller size', E49). Version R keeps the house defaults. Not ours: Fleckenstein's wide 'much more room' stop, ChartSchool's 4% trailing stop, Qullamaggie's 10/20-day target except as an option under D-013.

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop two cents over the rejection day's high (up to 5%), no trims, no breakeven, no trail; Version R's rule on all 2,630 liquid names, 1984 to 2026 (first trigger 1997-02-27); the market reading, the RS mirror, the borrow rule and the earnings mirror not applied. Of the 359 hits, 311 were stopped at some point in the window (262 before reaching 3R, 49 after reaching 3R, 14 of those after 5R), 42 had reached 3R and were unstopped at the window's end, and 6 ended under 3R unstopped; the groups overlap with the 51 that reached 5R (14 stopped later, 37 not) (corrected 2026-11-10 against the bars).

app_rule_gap_day_close_short_2005_2026.note: 988 liquid stocks with cached earnings dates, daily bars, house management mirrored; about 40 slices tested, so one or two can look positive by chance

failures.why: the 2015-08-05 gap came one session off the top on 10x volume, the kind he cut as 'just an earnings breakdown'; the bounce to the 20-day was rejected, but the trigger day was the low of the move and the stock reversed up through the stop at once (best 0.0R).

a textbook 35% gap on 27x volume (2020-08-19); the 20-day rejection came after 24 sessions with the stock already 40% off its high; 1.3R, then a rally through the stop. After a drop that large the 20-day sits far under the zone: shorting late, and Bulkowski's big drops bounce.

rejected at the 20-day after 19 to 23 sessions with a 1.3% stop, stopped at once (best 0.0R) in a strong general uptrend; the stock under its own 200-day satisfied B26, but the Red or Orange reading was not met.
the same shape as CIEN two months later: a 2.4% stop, stopped at once in a strong market. The scan did not check the market; the short needs its help.

Version P: day 2 opened 9.3% under Wednesday's close after the climax; Bracco's '3 failed attempts over 2 sessions'; the next session it fell further, then on 2026-01-20 it opened over the day-2 high.

gap 2021-04-21 (earnings, -7.4% on 6.2x), rejected at the gap zone after 8 sessions, a 2.8% stop; 1.86R by day 11 and never 3R; the close went back over the 20-day EMA on day 12 (the trail covers there) and the fixed stop went on day 36 on the close back over the 200-day (bg.inv_200).

examples.limits: The earnings database is complete only from about 2005, so VRSN and OI are classed as news gaps on the absence of a report. None of the ten is an ETF. The ten are the scan's winners chosen for clarity and spread; the base rate is the honest number. Survivors only, so delisted collapses are thin. The 39 bank drafts were ranked by what happened next (gap_held first) and are not a sample.

near_misses.why: the rejection day closed 5.9% above the 200-day SMA: a pullback in a leader, not a short; stopped at 0R.
the gap day opened -6.0% but closed down only 4.2%, at 70% of its range (rule: down 5% or more in the lower half): a gap bought back the same day, closer to a News Failure; stopped at 0R.
the rejection day closed at 82% of its range (rule: the lower half): a strong bounce with buyers in control; stopped at 0R.
the open was 2.1% (0.89 ATR) under the prior close (rule: at least 1 ATR or 4%): an ordinary down day with no gap zone; 0.2R then stopped.

conflicts: Sources: the card cites the dossier's own section 11 numbers (S1 Fleckenstein, S4 ChartSchool gaps, S7 Bulkowski gaps, S11 dead-cat bounce, S22 the UCT Substack, S23 the repo files, S24 the bars). Nobody originated 'bear gap off the highs'; the dossier's [originator] tag marks the authors of the named neighbouring setups (Fleckenstein's gap-down short), and the card follows that.

Today's house position against the card's short: TRADE_PLANS.md and course V.05 say the fall is measured, not traded, while Hard mode lists 'Bear gap' as its one short. The card records both; Version R and Version P are the dossier's measured short side, pending D-001.

Top or downtrend: ChartSchool's breakaway gap comes after 'an extended top'; Fleckenstein wants stocks 'already in major declines' below both averages; Bulkowski's bad-earnings short does best near the yearly low; the owner wants 'off the highs' and not 'downtrend gaps'. The card takes the owner's, with B26 then pushing the short to the later retest under the 200-day.

Short the gap or the bounce: ChartSchool's intraday method and Bracco's day-2 variant short the gap day; Fleckenstein, Bulkowski and the owner wait for the bounce and its rejection. The card takes the bounce (Version R) and keeps the gap-day short only as Version P.

Where the stop goes: over the gap day's high (the evidence tables; median 4.2%, 25% on VRNS), over the prior day's low or broken support (Fleckenstein), a few cents above the gap (Bulkowski), a 4% trailing stop (ChartSchool). The card takes the trigger candle's high within 3% (D-008).

News or no news: Fleckenstein and Stockbee require a catalyst; Savor and Chan find drift after news and reversal after no-news shocks; the owner rejected the earnings collapses he saw. The test's only positive slice was those collapses (+0.36R, 268 trades, one of about 40 slices, mostly above the 200-day). The card excludes the one-day collapse off a fresh high and flags the slice (D-025).

Gap size and volume: by eye (Fleckenstein), any full gap (ChartSchool), 1 standard deviation (QuantRocket), 15%+ (Bulkowski's dead-cat bounce), 5% and 2x (the app). The card takes 1 ATR or 4% with 1.5x volume; DECISIONS D-099's default makes volume a cue (the owner's SNDK gaps had 1.3x and 0.9x).

The gap definition: the app's full daily window against UCT's overnight gaps (BE, GLW, MRNA, SNDK were not full windows). The card takes the overnight gap with a floor and keeps the window as the stricter grade (D-099).
Which line: the course says the gap day's high; the overlay labels the prior day's low. The card draws the zone as one band (D-100).

The 200-day: 61% of the app's events close above it on the gap day and every UCT-named example but MPWR; B26 forbids those shorts unless parabolic. Whether B26's exception covers Bracco's day-2 variant, which lacks the climax-day gap up his main setup requires, is the owner's call (D-009).

Market: Fleckenstein wants a falling index and Bulkowski a bear market; the test found the gap-day close short did worse with SPY under its 200-day, and the scan's CIEN and CHKP failed in a strong uptrend. The card keeps D46's Red or Orange reading and says the short needs the market's help.

The evidence replay (measure_rules.py) counts the fill day's own low as profit on close entries, so the atlas's 1R 66% and 2R 44% overstate the gap-day close short (the dossier's own test: 48% and 31%). Owner question 12 in the dossier (D-028 in Part D) asks whether to fix it for every setup.
Bracco's C31 exemption: a stock gapping off its highs is usually still strong on RS; the card keeps C31's short mirror for Version R and asks whether the bear gap counts as mean reversion (D-009).
The Version P burst count (3 of 4 boxes) is the parabolic short card's number, not this dossier's; the dossier says only 'the more boxes checked, the stronger'.
